title: The Spirit and Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Spirit and Christ teaches that the Holy Spirit bears witness to Jesus, empowered His earthly ministry, and now glorifies Him by applying His saving work to believers.
summary: The Spirit and Christ teaches that the Holy Spirit bears witness to Jesus, empowered His earthly ministry, and now glorifies Him by applying His saving work to believers.
christFocus: The Spirit’s ministry is Christ-centered. He points to the Son, magnifies the Son, unites believers to the Son, and forms the character of the Son in God’s people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Holy Spirit is deeply involved in the mission of Christ. Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit, anointed by the Spirit, empowered for ministry, and vindicated in resurrection power.

The Spirit’s work does not compete with Christ’s glory. Jesus said the Spirit would glorify Him. This means the Spirit’s true ministry leads people to the truth, grace, lordship, and saving work of Jesus.

The Spirit applies what Christ accomplished. He gives life, unites believers to Christ, assures them of adoption, sanctifies them, and strengthens them to bear witness to the risen Lord.

A biblical view of the Spirit must therefore be Christ-centered. Spiritual experience that moves away from Jesus, His cross, His resurrection, His Word, or His commands is not the Spirit’s faithful work.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people either neglect the Spirit or make the Spirit’s work about power and experience detached from Christ. Scripture keeps the focus clear: the Spirit glorifies Jesus.

This doctrine helps believers test spiritual claims. The Spirit does not make Christ smaller; He makes Christ known, treasured, obeyed, and proclaimed.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask the Holy Spirit to keep your heart centered on Jesus. Seek spiritual life that leads to greater trust in Christ, deeper obedience to Christ, clearer worship of Christ, and bolder witness to Christ. Reject any spirituality that separates the Spirit from the Savior He glorifies.
